## Functions
#SHG_Setup
This function prepares the input file (input_r.txt) for the simulation executable. It accepts parameters like Sex, YOB, Population, and optional values such as Seed, Race, Path, and Version. The function modifies a template file, updates it with the specified values, and writes the customized file to the simulation directory.
 
```{r}
SHG_Setup <- function(Sex, YOB, Population, 
                      Seed = 1, Race = 0, Path = "SHG6.3.4", Version = 2023) {
  
  # Validate inputs
  if (!Version %in% c(2023, 2017)) {
    stop("Version must be 2023 or 2017.")
  }
  
  # Determine the file paths based on the Version
  prob_paths <- if (Version == 2023) {
    list(
      INIT_PROB = "SHG6.3.4/data/06_21_2023/lbc_shg_initiation06212023.txt",
      CESS_PROB = "SHG6.3.4/data/06_21_2023/lbc_shg_cessation06212023.txt",
      OCD_PROB  = "SHG6.3.4/data/06_21_2023/lbc_smokehist_ac_mortality_02212016.txt",
      CPD_DATA  = "SHG6.3.4/data/06_21_2023/lbc_shg_cpd06212023.txt"
    )
  } else {
    list(
      INIT_PROB = "SHG6.3.4/data/05_03_2017/lbc_shg_initiation05032017.txt",
      CESS_PROB = "SHG6.3.4/data/05_03_2017/lbc_shg_cessation05032017.txt",
      OCD_PROB  = "SHG6.3.4/data/05_03_2017/lbc_smokehist_ac_mortality_02212016.txt",
      CPD_DATA  = "SHG6.3.4/data/05_03_2017/lbc_shg_cpd05032017.txt"
    )
  }
  
  # Path to the input template
  input_template_path <- file.path(Path, "SHG_input_temp.txt")
  if (!file.exists(input_template_path)) {
    stop(paste("Template file not found at:", input_template_path))
  }
  
  # Read the input template
  input_text <- readLines(input_template_path)
  
  # Replace placeholders in the template
  modified_text <- input_text %>%
    gsub("{seed1}", Seed, ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("{seed2}", Seed, ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("{seed3}", Seed, ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("{seed4}", Seed, ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("RACE=0", paste0("RACE=", Race), ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("SEX=0", paste0("SEX=", Sex), ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("{cohort}", YOB, ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("REPEAT=100000", paste0("REPEAT=", Population), ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("INIT_PROB=SHG6.3.4/data/06_21_2023/lbc_shg_initiation06212023.txt", 
         paste0("INIT_PROB=", prob_paths$INIT_PROB), ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("CESS_PROB=SHG6.3.4/data/06_21_2023/lbc_shg_cessation06212023.txt", 
         paste0("CESS_PROB=", prob_paths$CESS_PROB), ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("OCD_PROB=SHG6.3.4/data/06_21_2023/lbc_smokehist_oc_mortality_02212016.txt", 
         paste0("OCD_PROB=", prob_paths$OCD_PROB), ., fixed = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("CPD_DATA=SHG6.3.4/data/06_21_2023/lbc_shg_cpd06212023.txt", 
         paste0("CPD_DATA=", prob_paths$CPD_DATA), ., fixed = TRUE)
  
  # Path to the output file
  output_file_path <- file.path(Path, "input_r.txt")
  
  # Write the modified text to the output file
  writeLines(modified_text, output_file_path)
  
  # Notify the user
  message("Modified input file written to: ", output_file_path)
}
```


#SHG_Run
This function executes the simulation executable (lbc_smokehist_win.exe) using a specified input file (input_r.txt). After running the simulation, it checks for the existence of the output file (output_r.out) to confirm success. The function reports an error if the output file is not generated.

```{r}
SHG_Run <- function(Path = "SHG6.3.4") {
  # Define paths for the input file, executable, and output file
  input_file <- file.path(Path, "input_r.txt")
  exe_file <- file.path(Path, "lbc_smokehist_win.exe")
  output_file <- file.path("output_r.out")
  
  # Check if the executable and input file exist
  if (!file.exists(exe_file)) {
    stop(paste("Executable not found at:", exe_file))
  }
  if (!file.exists(input_file)) {
    stop(paste("Input file not found at:", input_file))
  }
  
  # Build the command to execute
  command <- paste(shQuote(exe_file), shQuote(input_file))
  
  # Run the command
  message("Running command: ", command)
  system(command, wait = TRUE)
  
  # Check for the output file
  if (file.exists(output_file)) {
    message("Success: Output file created at ", output_file)
  } else {
    stop("Error: Output file not found after running the executable.")
  }
}
```


#SHG_Output
This function reads and processes the output file (output_r.out) generated by the simulation executable. It extracts individual-level simulation results such as smoking initiation, cessation, and death ages, as well as yearly smoking data (cigarettes per day). The results are returned in a structured dataframe for further analysis.

```{r}
SHG_Output <- function(outfile = "output_r.out") {
  # Check if the output file exists
  if (!file.exists(outfile)) {
    stop(paste("Output file not found:", outfile))
  }
  
  # Read the contents of the output file
  file_lines <- readLines(outfile)
  
  # Find the <RUN> section
  run_start <- grep("<RUN>", file_lines)
  run_end <- grep("</RUN>", file_lines)
  
  if (length(run_start) == 0 || length(run_end) == 0) {
    stop("The <RUN> section is missing in the output file.")
  }
  
  # Extract the lines within the <RUN> section
  run_lines <- file_lines[(run_start + 1):(run_end - 1)]
  
  # Initialize an empty list to hold the data for each individual
  rows <- list()
  
  # Loop through each line in the <RUN> section
  for (line in run_lines) {
    # Split the line by semicolons
    parts <- unlist(strsplit(line, ";"))
    
    # Extract the first six values
    race <- as.numeric(parts[1])
    sex <- as.numeric(parts[2])
    yob <- as.numeric(parts[3])
    initiation_age <- as.numeric(parts[4])
    cessation_age <- as.numeric(parts[5])
    death_age <- as.numeric(parts[6])
    if (death_age==-999){
      death_age <- 109
    }
    
    # Initialize a vector to store CPD values for ages 1 to 110
    cpd_values <- rep(0, 110)
    
    # Check if there are CPD values in the line
    if (length(parts) > 6) {
      # Extract the remaining values after the first six
      age_cpd_pairs <- as.numeric(parts[7:length(parts)])
      
      # Loop through the age-CPD pairs
      for (i in seq(1, length(age_cpd_pairs), by = 2)) {
        age <- age_cpd_pairs[i]
        cpd <- age_cpd_pairs[i + 1]
        
        # Stop if we've passed cessation or death age
        if (!is.na(cessation_age) && age > cessation_age && cessation_age!=-999) break
        if (!is.na(death_age) && age > death_age) break
        
        # Assign the CPD value for the given age
        cpd_values[age] <- cpd
      }
    }
    
    # Combine the data into a row
    row <- c(race, sex, yob, initiation_age, cessation_age, death_age, cpd_values)
    rows <- append(rows, list(row))
  }
  
  # Create a dataframe from the rows
  column_names <- c("Race", "Sex", "YOB", "Initiation_Age", "Cessation_Age", "Death_Age", 1:110)
  SHG_out <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows))
  colnames(SHG_out) <- column_names
  
  return(SHG_out)
}
```


#SHG_rslts_ini
This function initializes an empty dataframe for storing simulation results. The dataframe contains columns for key variables such as Sex, Race, YOB, Age, Initiation_Age, Cessation_Age, Eversmoker, Smokenow, CigsPerDay, Pack_Years, and Smoking_Years. It provides a structured container to accumulate and manage simulation data.

```{r}
SHG_rslts_ini <- function() {
    # Initialize aggr_out with specified columns
    df_name <- data.frame(
      Sex = integer(),
      Race = integer(),
      YOB = integer(),
      Age = integer(),
      Initiation_Age = integer(),
      Cessation_Age = integer(),
      Quit_Age = integer(),
      Eversmoker = integer(),
      Smokenow = integer(),
      CigsPerDay = numeric(),
      Pack_Years_Minusone = numeric(),
      Pack_Years = numeric(),
      Smoking_Years = integer(),
      Smoking_Years_Minusone = integer(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    return(df_name)
}
```


#SHG_Aggr
This function aggregates simulation results (shgrun_out) into a dataframe (aggr_out) for analysis. It calculates individual attributes like smoking status, cigarettes per day, pack years, and smoking years based on simulation inputs and outputs. The function also ensures that only individuals alive at the data collection year are included. If aggr_out is not already initialized, it creates it.

```{r}
SHG_Aggr <- function(shgrun_out, aggr_out, collection_year, exclude_deceased = "On") {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(shgrun_out))) {
    # Extract values from shgrun_out
    row <- shgrun_out[i, ]
    sex <- row$Sex
    race <- row$Race
    yob <- row$YOB
    initiation_age <- row$Initiation_Age
    cessation_age <- row$Cessation_Age
    death_age <- row$Death_Age

    # Calculate age
    age <- collection_year - yob

    # Exclude deceased individuals if the option is "On"
    if (exclude_deceased == "On" && age > death_age) {
      next  # Skip this individual
    }

    # Determine if the individual is an EverSmoker
    eversmoker <- ifelse(initiation_age == -999 | initiation_age > age, 0, 1)

    # Initialize derived values
    smokenow <- 0
    cigs_per_day <- 0
    pack_years <- 0
    pack_years_minusone <- 0
    smoking_years <- 0
    smoking_years_minusone <- 0
    quit_age <- 0
    
    # Check if the individual has smoked all the way through their life
    if (cessation_age < 0 & initiation_age > 0) {
      cessation_age <- death_age
    }
    
    if (eversmoker == 1) {
      # Check if the individual is currently smoking
      if (age > initiation_age & age <= cessation_age) {
        smokenow <- 1
      }
      
      quit_age <- cessation_age+1

      # Extract smoking data from ages 1 to current age
      smoking_data <- as.numeric(row[7:(6 + age)])  # Columns 7 to (6 + age)

      # Calculate non-zero average for CigsPerDay
      cigs_per_day <- mean(smoking_data[smoking_data > 0], na.rm = TRUE)

      # Calculate Pack Years (sum of all smoking data divided by 20)
      pack_years <- sum(smoking_data, na.rm = TRUE) / 20

      # Calculate Smoking Years
      if (!is.na(cessation_age)) {
        if (cessation_age >= age) {
          smoking_years <- age - initiation_age + 1  # Individual hasn't quit smoking yet
          smoking_years_minusone <- age - initiation_age
        } else if (cessation_age > initiation_age) {
          smoking_years <- cessation_age - initiation_age + 1 # Normal case
          smoking_years_minusone <- cessation_age - initiation_age
        }
      }
      
      # Calculate Pack Years (smoking years * CPD/20)
      pack_years_minusone <- smoking_years_minusone * cigs_per_day / 20
    }

    # Append the individual's data to aggr_out
    aggr_out <- rbind(aggr_out, data.frame(
      Sex = sex,
      Race = race,
      YOB = yob,
      Age = age,
      Initiation_Age = initiation_age,
      Cessation_Age = cessation_age,
      Quit_Age = quit_age,
      Eversmoker = eversmoker,
      Smokenow = smokenow,
      CigsPerDay = cigs_per_day,
      Pack_Years = pack_years,
      Pack_Years_Minusone = pack_years_minusone,
      Smoking_Years = smoking_years,
      Smoking_Years_Minusone = smoking_years_minusone,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }
  return(aggr_out)
}
```


#SHGdat2BY
This function creates a birth year report from simulation results. It takes a dataframe containing simulation results (shgdata) and groups the data by YOB (Year of Birth). For each year of birth, it calculates the count of Females and Males and returns a summarized dataframe ordered by YOB.

```{r}
SHGdat2BY <- function(shgdata) {
  # Check if required columns are present
  required_columns <- c("YOB", "Sex")
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, colnames(shgdata))
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(paste("The following required columns are missing from 'shgdata':", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  # Check if YOB and Sex columns contain valid data types
  if (!is.numeric(shgdata$YOB)) {
    stop("Column 'YOB' must be numeric.")
  }
  if (!is.numeric(shgdata$Sex)) {
    stop("Column 'Sex' must be numeric.")
  }
  
  # Ensure no negative or nonsensical years in YOB
  if (any(shgdata$YOB < 1800 | shgdata$YOB > 2100, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    warning("Some 'YOB' values are outside a reasonable range (1800-2100). These will be included unless removed beforehand.")
  }
  
  # Summarize data by YOB
  SHGBY <- shgdata %>%
    group_by(YOB) %>%
    summarise(
      Females = sum(Sex == 1, na.rm = TRUE),  # Count of females
      Males = sum(Sex == 0, na.rm = TRUE)    # Count of males
    ) %>%
    arrange(YOB)  # Sort by YOB
  
  # Return the summarized dataframe
  return(SHGBY)
}
```


#sufftrgt
This function scales the values in a birth year report (byrdata) to create a target dataset. It multiplies the counts of Females and Males in the input dataframe by a coverage factor (default is 10) and returns the scaled dataset.

```{r}
sufftrgt <- function(byrdata, coverage = 10) {
  # Check for required columns
  required_columns <- c("Females", "Males")
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, colnames(byrdata))
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(paste("The following required columns are missing from 'byrdata':", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")))
  }

  # Scale Females and Males by the coverage factor
  byrtrgt <- byrdata
  byrtrgt$Females <- coverage * byrdata$Females
  byrtrgt$Males <- coverage * byrdata$Males
  
  # Return the modified dataframe
  return(byrtrgt)
}
```


#suff_shortage
This function calculates the shortage of individuals in a birth year dataset relative to a target dataset. It takes two dataframes: byrrslts (results) and byrtrgt (target). For each YOB-gender combination, if the results fall short of the target, it calculates the difference; otherwise, it assigns zero. The output matches the structure of the target dataset (byrtrgt).

```{r}
suff_shortage <- function(byrrslts, byrtrgt) {
  # Check for required columns
  required_columns <- c("YOB", "Females", "Males")
  missing_byrrslts <- setdiff(required_columns, colnames(byrrslts))
  missing_byrtrgt <- setdiff(required_columns, colnames(byrtrgt))
  if (length(missing_byrrslts) > 0) {
    stop(paste("The following required columns are missing from 'byrrslts':", paste(missing_byrrslts, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  if (length(missing_byrtrgt) > 0) {
    stop(paste("The following required columns are missing from 'byrtrgt':", paste(missing_byrtrgt, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  # Merge the two dataframes by YOB, keeping all rows from byrtrgt
  combined <- merge(
    byrtrgt, byrrslts, 
    by = "YOB", 
    all.x = TRUE,  # Keep all rows from byrtrgt
    suffixes = c("_trgt", "_rslts")
  )
  
  # Replace NA values in byrrslts columns with 0
  combined$Females_rslts[is.na(combined$Females_rslts)] <- 0
  combined$Males_rslts[is.na(combined$Males_rslts)] <- 0
  
  # Calculate shortage
  combined$Females_shortage <- pmax(combined$Females_trgt - combined$Females_rslts, 0)
  combined$Males_shortage <- pmax(combined$Males_trgt - combined$Males_rslts, 0)
  
  # Create the output dataframe with the same structure as byrtrgt
  byrrem <- combined[, c("YOB", "Females_shortage", "Males_shortage")]
  colnames(byrrem) <- c("YOB", "Females", "Males")
  
  return(byrrem)
}
```


#SHGbyr
This function runs simulations to meet population targets specified in a birth year dataset (BYr). For each YOB-gender combination, it prepares input files, runs simulations, processes outputs, and aggregates results into AggData. It uses looping to process all rows and genders in BYr and dynamically updates the aggregated results.

```{r}
SHGbyr <- function(BYr, prcssyr, seed, exclude_deceased = "On") {
  # Input Validation ---------------------------------------------------------
  if (!all(c("YOB") %in% colnames(BYr))) {
    stop("The 'BYr' dataframe must include a 'YOB' column.")
  }
  if (ncol(BYr) < 3) {
    stop("The 'BYr' dataframe must have at least three columns: 'YOB', 'Females', and 'Males'.")
  }

  # Initialize an empty dataframe for aggregated data
  AggData <- SHG_rslts_ini()
  
  # Outer loop: Iterate over each row in the 'BYr' dataframe
  for (i in 1:nrow(BYr)) {
    # Extract the birth year for the current row
    YBirth <- BYr[i, "YOB"]
    
    # Inner loop: Iterate over genders (j = 1 for males, j = 2 for females)
    for (j in c(1, 2)) {
      # Extract the population for the current year and gender
      poprun <- BYr[i, j + 1]
      
      # Skip if the population is zero or NA
      if (is.na(poprun) || poprun == 0) {
        next
      }
      
      # Map gender: j = 1 -> gender = 1 (female), j = 2 -> gender = 0 (male)
      gender <- 2 - j
      
      # Set up the simulation input
      SHG_Setup(Sex = gender, YOB = YBirth, Population = poprun, Seed = i * seed + j)
      
      # Run the simulation
      SHG_Run()
      
      # Process the simulation output
      SHGout <- SHG_Output()
      
      # Aggregate the simulation output
      AggData <- SHG_Aggr(SHGout, AggData, prcssyr, exclude_deceased)  # Pass exclude_deceased
    }
  }
  
  # Return the aggregated data
  return(AggData)
}
```


#SHGbyr_extend
This function extends the aggregated results (AggData) until population shortages specified in BYr are resolved. It calculates shortages using suff_shortage and runs additional simulations for any YOB-gender combination that falls short. The process continues until all shortages are eliminated, and the function returns the updated AggData.

```{r}
SHGbyr_extend <- function(AggData, BYr, prcssyr, seed, exclude_deceased = "On") {
  # Input Validation ---------------------------------------------------------
  if (!all(c("YOB", "Females", "Males") %in% colnames(BYr))) {
    stop("The 'BYr' dataframe must include the columns: 'YOB', 'Females', and 'Males'.")
  }
  
  # Processing Loop ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 1: Initialize shortage calculation
  repeat {
    # Step 2: Get the current birth year report from AggData
    Aggbyr <- SHGdat2BY(AggData)
    
    # Step 3: Calculate the shortage
    newbyr <- suff_shortage(Aggbyr, BYr)
    
    # Check sufficiency criteria: All shortages must be zero
    if (all(newbyr$Females == 0 & newbyr$Males == 0)) {
      break  # Exit the loop when no shortages remain
    }
    
    # Step 4: Iterate over each row in 'newbyr'
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(newbyr))) {
      # Extract the birth year for the current row
      YBirth <- newbyr[i, "YOB"]
      
      # Inner loop: Iterate over genders (1 for females, 2 for males)
      for (j in c(1, 2)) {
        # Extract the population for the current year and gender
        poprun <- newbyr[i, j + 1]  # Column 2 is Females, Column 3 is Males
        
        # Skip if the population is zero or NA
        if (is.na(poprun) || poprun == 0) {
          next
        }
        
        # Map gender: 1 -> Female (1), 2 -> Male (0)
        gender <- 2 - j
        
        # Set up the simulation input
        SHG_Setup(Sex = gender, YOB = YBirth, Population = poprun, Seed = i * seed + j)
        
        # Run the simulation
        SHG_Run()
        
        # Process the simulation output
        SHGout <- SHG_Output()
        
        # Aggregate the simulation output, incorporating exclude_deceased
        AggData <- SHG_Aggr(SHGout, AggData, prcssyr, exclude_deceased = exclude_deceased)
      }
    }
    
    # Increment the seed to ensure variability in simulations
    seed <- seed + 1
  }
  
  # Return the aggregated data ------------------------------------------------
  return(AggData)
}
```


#sample_SHG
This function performs random sampling from simulation results (SHG_rslts) based on a target dataset (BYr). For each YOB-gender combination in BYr, it filters eligible candidates from SHG_rslts and selects a random sample matching the target size. The sampled entries are aggregated and returned as a new dataframe.

```{r}
sample_SHG <- function(SHG_rslts, BYr, seed) {
  # Input Validation ---------------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(SHG_rslts)) {
    stop("Input 'SHG_rslts' must be a dataframe.")
  }
  if (!all(c("YOB", "Females", "Males") %in% colnames(BYr))) {
    stop("The 'BYr' dataframe must include columns: 'YOB', 'Females', and 'Males'.")
  }
  if (!is.numeric(seed) || length(seed) != 1) {
    stop("Input 'seed' must be a single numeric value.")
  }
  
  # Set the random seed for reproducibility
  set.seed(seed)
  
  # Initialize an empty dataframe to store the output samples
  sampled_data <- SHG_rslts[0, ]  # Empty dataframe with same structure as SHG_rslts
  
  # Sampling Loop ------------------------------------------------------------
  for (i in 1:nrow(BYr)) {
    # Extract the current YOB and sample populations
    current_yob <- as.numeric(BYr[i, "YOB"])
    female_pop <- as.numeric(BYr[i, "Females"])
    male_pop <- as.numeric(BYr[i, "Males"])
    
    # Sample females
    if (female_pop > 0) {
      female_candidates <- SHG_rslts[which(SHG_rslts$YOB == current_yob & SHG_rslts$Sex == 1), ]
      if (nrow(female_candidates) == 0) {
        warning(paste("No female candidates for YOB =", current_yob))
      } else {
        female_pop <- min(female_pop, nrow(female_candidates))  # Adjust to available candidates
        female_sample <- female_candidates[sample(seq_len(nrow(female_candidates)), size = female_pop), ]
        sampled_data <- rbind(sampled_data, female_sample)
      }
    }
    
    # Sample males
    if (male_pop > 0) {
      male_candidates <- SHG_rslts[which(SHG_rslts$YOB == current_yob & SHG_rslts$Sex == 0), ]
      if (nrow(male_candidates) == 0) {
        warning(paste("No male candidates for YOB =", current_yob))
      } else {
        male_pop <- min(male_pop, nrow(male_candidates))  # Adjust to available candidates
        male_sample <- male_candidates[sample(seq_len(nrow(male_candidates)), size = male_pop), ]
        sampled_data <- rbind(sampled_data, male_sample)
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Return the sampled data --------------------------------------------------
  return(sampled_data)
}
```


#smpl2age
This function summarizes smoking-related metrics by Age and Sex for a given simulation sample or results dataframe. It calculates the percentage of Eversmoker and Smokenow individuals, as well as the average CigsPerDay, Pack_Years, and Smoking_Years for those who are Eversmoker == 1. The resulting dataframe provides an age-sex breakdown of smoking behaviors and history.

```{r}
smpl2age <- function(data) {
  # Input Validation ---------------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("Input 'data' must be a dataframe.")
  }
  
  required_columns <- c("Age", "Sex", "Eversmoker", "Smokenow", 
                        "CigsPerDay", "Pack_Years", "Smoking_Years")
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, colnames(data))
  
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(paste("Missing required columns:", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  # Create a summary dataframe -----------------------------------------------
  summary_df <- data %>%
    group_by(Age, Sex) %>% 
    summarise(
      Total = n(),
      EverSmoker_Percentage = 100 * mean(Eversmoker == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      SmokeNow_Percentage = 100 * mean(Smokenow == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      CPD_Avg = mean(CigsPerDay[Eversmoker == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
      CPD_Std = sd(CigsPerDay[Eversmoker == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
      PY_Avg = mean(Pack_Years[Eversmoker == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
      PY_Std = sd(Pack_Years[Eversmoker == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
      SY_Avg = mean(Smoking_Years[Eversmoker == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
      SY_Std = sd(Smoking_Years[Eversmoker == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Age, Sex) %>%  # Sort by Age and Sex
    ungroup()
  
  # Return the summary dataframe ---------------------------------------------
  return(summary_df)
}
```


#dat2age
This function is designed for observed cohort data in this workflow. It transforms and prepares the data by:
Renaming key columns for consistency (Enrollment_Age to Age, etc.).
Recoding the Sex column (M → 0, F → 1).
Replacing missing values (NA) in Eversmoker and Smokenow with 0.
Calculating a new Smoking_Years column based on smoking history. Once the transformations are complete, the function calls smpl2age to generate a summarized dataframe showing smoking-related metrics by Age and Sex.

```{r}
dat2age <- function(data) {
  # Input Validation ---------------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("Input 'data' must be a dataframe.")
  }

  required_columns <- c("Enrollment_Age", "Sex", "RaceAnalysis", 
                        "EverSmoker", "SmokeNow", 
                        "PackYears", "AgeQuitSmoking", "AgeStartSmoking")
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, colnames(data))
  
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(paste("Missing required columns:", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")))
  }

  # Step 1: Replace NA in Eversmoker and Smokenow ----------------------------
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(
      EverSmoker = ifelse(is.na(EverSmoker), 0, EverSmoker),
      SmokeNow = ifelse(is.na(SmokeNow), 0, SmokeNow)
    )

  # Step 2: Rename columns ---------------------------------------------------
  data <- data %>%
    rename(
      Age = Enrollment_Age,
      Race = RaceAnalysis,
      Eversmoker = EverSmoker,
      Smokenow = SmokeNow,
      Pack_Years = PackYears
    )
  
  # Step 3: Recode Sex column ------------------------------------------------
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(Sex = case_when(
      Sex == "M" ~ 0,
      Sex == "F" ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ))

  # Step 4: Calculate Smoking_Years column -----------------------------------
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(Smoking_Years = case_when(
      Eversmoker == 0 ~ 0,
      Eversmoker == 1 & Smokenow == 0 ~ AgeQuitSmoking - AgeStartSmoking,
      Eversmoker == 1 & Smokenow == 1 ~ Age - AgeStartSmoking,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ))

  # Step 5: Call smpl2age ----------------------------------------------------
  summary_df <- smpl2age(data)

  # Return the summary dataframe ---------------------------------------------
  return(summary_df)
}
```


#aggregate_density
This function aggregates density estimates from multiple samples for a given variable, such as CigsPerDay, Pack_Years, or Smoking_Years. It calculates the mean density and confidence interval (CI) bounds for each bin (x value), summarizing distributional trends across samples. This approach avoids storing large raw datasets while retaining essential information about variability and central tendencies in the sampled distributions.

```{r}
aggregate_density <- function(dist_list, var_name, CI = 0.95) {
  # Combine density data for all repetitions into a single dataframe
  all_densities <- bind_rows(
    lapply(dist_list, function(d) data.frame(x = d[[var_name]]$x, y = d[[var_name]]$y)),
    .id = "Rep"
  )
  
  # Aggregate densities by x-values
  aggregated <- all_densities %>%
    group_by(x) %>%
    summarise(
      Mean = mean(y),
      Lower = quantile(y, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      Upper = quantile(y, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),
      .groups = "drop"  # Drop grouping to avoid warnings
    )
  
  return(aggregated)
}
```


#BYrf and BYrm
The BYrf and BYrm functions transform a BYr dataframe into gender-specific subsets while preserving the original structure.
  - BYrf: Retains the Females column and sets the Males column to 0, effectively creating a BYr structure representing only females.
  - BYrm: Retains the Males column and sets the Females column to 0, effectively creating a BYr structure representing only males.
Both functions ensure the YOB, Females, and Males columns are maintained for consistency.

```{r}
# Function to create a BYr structure with only females
BYrf <- function(BYr) {
  # Validate input
  if (!all(c("YOB", "Females", "Males") %in% colnames(BYr))) {
    stop("BYr must have columns: 'YOB', 'Females', and 'Males'.")
  }
  
  # Create a new BYr structure with Females intact and Males set to 0
  BYr_females <- BYr
  BYr_females$Males <- 0  # Set Males to 0
  return(BYr_females)
}

# Function to create a BYr structure with only males
BYrm <- function(BYr) {
  # Validate input
  if (!all(c("YOB", "Females", "Males") %in% colnames(BYr))) {
    stop("BYr must have columns: 'YOB', 'Females', and 'Males'.")
  }
  
  # Create a new BYr structure with Males intact and Females set to 0
  BYr_males <- BYr
  BYr_males$Females <- 0  # Set Females to 0
  return(BYr_males)
}
```


#rep_smpl_dist
This function performs repeated sampling from a dataset and tracks key variables (CigsPerDay, Pack_Years, Smoking_Years) and age-based smoking metrics (EverSmoker_Percentage, SmokeNow_Percentage). For each repetition, it calculates density distributions for ever-smokers and aggregates results into two dataframes: one with mean distributions and CI bounds, and another summarizing age-sex-specific smoking statistics with CI bounds. This function provides a robust framework for analyzing variability across samples.

```{r}
# Helper Function: Process Distributions for Eversmokers
process_distributions <- function(smpl) {
  smpl_ever <- smpl[smpl$Eversmoker == 1, ]
  
  list(
    CigsPerDay = density(smpl_ever$CigsPerDay, from = 0, to = 100, n = 512),
    Pack_Years = density(smpl_ever$Pack_Years, from = 0, to = 100, n = 512),
    Pack_Years_Minusone = density(smpl_ever$Pack_Years_Minusone, from = 0, to = 100, n = 512),
    Smoking_Years = density(smpl_ever$Smoking_Years, from = 0, to = 100, n = 512),
    Smoking_Years_Minusone = density(smpl_ever$Smoking_Years_Minusone, from = 0, to = 100, n = 512)
  )
}

# Main Function: rep_smpl_dist
rep_smpl_dist <- function(data, BYr, rep, CI = 0.95) {
  # Step 1: Initialize storage for distributions and age breakdown
  dist_list <- list(full = list(), female = list(), male = list())
  age_breakdown_list <- list()
  
  # Step 2: Main loop over repetitions
  for (seed in 1:rep) {
    # Sample once for the full population
    smpl_full <- sample_SHG(data, BYr, seed)
    
    # Filter subsets for female and male populations
    smpl_female <- smpl_full %>% filter(Sex == 1)
    smpl_male <- smpl_full %>% filter(Sex == 0)
    
    # Collect distributions for all three subpopulations
    dist_list$full[[seed]] <- process_distributions(smpl_full)
    dist_list$female[[seed]] <- process_distributions(smpl_female)
    dist_list$male[[seed]] <- process_distributions(smpl_male)
    
    # Age breakdown (only for full population)
    age_breakdown_list[[seed]] <- smpl2age(smpl_full)
  }
  
  # Step 3: Aggregate distributions across repetitions
  dist_aggregated <- list(
    full = list(
      CigsPerDay = aggregate_density(dist_list$full, "CigsPerDay", CI),
      Pack_Years = aggregate_density(dist_list$full, "Pack_Years", CI),
      Pack_Years_Minusone = aggregate_density(dist_list$full, "Pack_Years_Minusone", CI),
      Smoking_Years = aggregate_density(dist_list$full, "Smoking_Years", CI),
      Smoking_Years_Minusone = aggregate_density(dist_list$full, "Smoking_Years_Minusone", CI)
    ),
    female = list(
      CigsPerDay = aggregate_density(dist_list$female, "CigsPerDay", CI),
      Pack_Years = aggregate_density(dist_list$female, "Pack_Years", CI),
      Pack_Years_Minusone = aggregate_density(dist_list$female, "Pack_Years_Minusone", CI),
      Smoking_Years = aggregate_density(dist_list$female, "Smoking_Years", CI),
      Smoking_Years_Minusone = aggregate_density(dist_list$female, "Smoking_Years_Minusone", CI)
    ),
    male = list(
      CigsPerDay = aggregate_density(dist_list$male, "CigsPerDay", CI),
      Pack_Years = aggregate_density(dist_list$male, "Pack_Years", CI),
      Pack_Years_Minusone = aggregate_density(dist_list$male, "Pack_Years_Minusone", CI),
      Smoking_Years = aggregate_density(dist_list$male, "Smoking_Years", CI),
      Smoking_Years_Minusone = aggregate_density(dist_list$male, "Smoking_Years_Minusone", CI)
    )
  )
  
  # Step 4: Aggregate age breakdowns
  age_results <- bind_rows(age_breakdown_list, .id = "Rep") %>%
    group_by(Age, Sex) %>%
    summarise(
      EverSmoker_Mean = mean(EverSmoker_Percentage),
      EverSmoker_Lower = quantile(EverSmoker_Percentage, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      EverSmoker_Upper = quantile(EverSmoker_Percentage, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),
      SmokeNow_Mean = mean(SmokeNow_Percentage),
      SmokeNow_Lower = quantile(SmokeNow_Percentage, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      SmokeNow_Upper = quantile(SmokeNow_Percentage, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # Return aggregated results
  return(list(Distributions = dist_aggregated, AgeBreakdown = age_results))
}
```


#extr_prvlnc_smpld_rslts
The extr_prvlnc_smpld_rslts function extracts and formats the age-based prevalence and smoking metrics from the output of the rep_smpl_dist function. It focuses on the AgeBreakdown component of the input, ensuring the necessary columns (e.g., EverSmoker_Mean, SmokeNow_Mean, and their confidence intervals) are present and correctly formatted. The function directly selects these columns, reorders them for clarity, and arranges the data by age and sex. The resulting dataframe includes columns for age, sex, and smoking-related metrics with their mean and confidence interval bounds, making it ready for further analysis or visualization.

```{r}
extr_prvlnc_smpld_rslts <- function(smpld_SHG_rslts, CI = 0.95) {
  # Input Validation ---------------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.list(smpld_SHG_rslts) || !"AgeBreakdown" %in% names(smpld_SHG_rslts)) {
    stop("Input 'smpld_SHG_rslts' must be a list containing an 'AgeBreakdown' component.")
  }

  # Extract AgeBreakdown -----------------------------------------------------
  age_breakdown <- smpld_SHG_rslts$AgeBreakdown

  # Check for necessary columns ----------------------------------------------
  required_cols <- c("Age", "Sex", "EverSmoker_Mean", "SmokeNow_Mean", 
                     "EverSmoker_Lower", "EverSmoker_Upper", 
                     "SmokeNow_Lower", "SmokeNow_Upper")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, colnames(age_breakdown))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(paste("Missing columns in 'AgeBreakdown':", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
  }

  # Assign confidence interval columns directly ------------------------------
  result <- age_breakdown %>%
    select(
      Age, Sex,
      EverSmoker_Mean, 
      EverSmoker_Lower, EverSmoker_Upper,
      SmokeNow_Mean, 
      SmokeNow_Lower, SmokeNow_Upper
    ) %>%
    arrange(Age, Sex)  # Optional: ensure ordering by Age and Sex

  # Return the formatted dataframe -------------------------------------------
  return(result)
}
```


#extr_dist_smpld_rslts
The extr_dist_smpld_rslts function focuses on extracting and consolidating the distributions of smoking-related variables (CigsPerDay, Pack_Years, and Smoking_Years) from the Distributions component of the rep_smpl_dist output. It ensures that the input structure includes required columns (x, Mean, Lower, Upper) for each variable. The function combines these distributions into a single dataframe and reshapes it into a wide format, where each variable’s distribution is represented with its mean and confidence interval bounds. This structured output enables easy comparisons of variable distributions and is ready for detailed statistical analysis or visualization.

```{r}
extr_dist_smpld_rslts <- function(smpld_SHG_rslts, population = "full", CI = 0.95) {
  # Validate the population input
  if (!population %in% c("full", "female", "male")) {
    stop("Invalid population input. Choose from 'full', 'female', or 'male'.")
  }
  
  # Access the specific subpopulation distributions
  dist <- smpld_SHG_rslts$Distributions[[population]]
  
  # Combine distributions into a single dataframe in the desired format
  aggregated_dist <- tibble(
    x = dist$CigsPerDay$x,  # x-values are the same across all distributions
    CigsPerDay_Mean = dist$CigsPerDay$Mean,
    CigsPerDay_Lower = dist$CigsPerDay$Lower,
    CigsPerDay_Upper = dist$CigsPerDay$Upper,
    Pack_Years_Mean = dist$Pack_Years$Mean,
    Pack_Years_Lower = dist$Pack_Years$Lower,
    Pack_Years_Upper = dist$Pack_Years$Upper,
    Pack_Years_M1_Mean = dist$Pack_Years_Minusone$Mean,
    Pack_Years_M1_Lower = dist$Pack_Years_Minusone$Lower,
    Pack_Years_M1_Upper = dist$Pack_Years_Minusone$Upper,
    Smoking_Years_Mean = dist$Smoking_Years$Mean,
    Smoking_Years_Lower = dist$Smoking_Years$Lower,
    Smoking_Years_Upper = dist$Smoking_Years$Upper,
    Smoking_Years_M1_Mean = dist$Smoking_Years_Minusone$Mean,
    Smoking_Years_M1_Lower = dist$Smoking_Years_Minusone$Lower,
    Smoking_Years_M1_Upper = dist$Smoking_Years_Minusone$Upper
  )
  
  # Return the aggregated dataframe
  return(aggregated_dist)
}
```


#make_prvlnc_plot
Creates a prevalence plot comparing SHG simulations and data by age, sex, and smoking status. Includes confidence intervals, customizable legends, and titles. Inputs: SHG and data prevalence, target ("EverSmoker" or "SmokeNow"), CI level, and display options for legends and subtitles. Outputs a ggplot2 object.

```{r}
# Helper function for prevalence plots
make_prevalence_plot <- function(SHG_prvlnc, dat_prvlnc, target, CI = 95, legend = "On", subtitle = NULL) {
  # Validate inputs
  if (!target %in% c("EverSmoker", "SmokeNow")) {
    stop("Invalid target. Choose either 'EverSmoker' or 'SmokeNow'.")
  }
  required_cols <- c("Age", "Sex", paste0(target, "_Mean"), paste0(target, "_Lower"), paste0(target, "_Upper"))
  if (!all(required_cols %in% colnames(SHG_prvlnc))) {
    stop(paste("SHG_prvlnc must contain the necessary columns for", target, "analysis."))
  }
  if (!all(c("Age", "Sex", paste0(target, "_Percentage")) %in% colnames(dat_prvlnc))) {
    stop(paste("dat_prvlnc must contain the necessary columns for", target, "analysis."))
  }

  # Split data by gender
  SHG_male <- SHG_prvlnc[SHG_prvlnc$Sex == 0, ]
  SHG_female <- SHG_prvlnc[SHG_prvlnc$Sex == 1, ]
  dat_male <- dat_prvlnc[dat_prvlnc$Sex == 0, ]
  dat_female <- dat_prvlnc[dat_prvlnc$Sex == 1, ]

  # Define labels for legend
  CI_label_m <- paste0("Males (", CI, "% CI)")
  CI_label_f <- paste0("Females (", CI, "% CI)")
  y_label <- paste(target, "Percentage")

  # Set up plot title
  plottitle <- if (!is.null(subtitle)) subtitle else NULL

  # Create the plot
  plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_ribbon(
      data = SHG_male,
      aes(x = Age, ymin = .data[[paste0(target, "_Lower")]], ymax = .data[[paste0(target, "_Upper")]], fill = CI_label_m),
      alpha = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_ribbon(
      data = SHG_female,
      aes(x = Age, ymin = .data[[paste0(target, "_Lower")]], ymax = .data[[paste0(target, "_Upper")]], fill = CI_label_f),
      alpha = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = SHG_male,
      aes(x = Age, y = .data[[paste0(target, "_Mean")]], color = "Males (SHG)"),
      size = 1
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = SHG_female,
      aes(x = Age, y = .data[[paste0(target, "_Mean")]], color = "Females (SHG)"),
      size = 1
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = dat_male,
      aes(x = Age, y = .data[[paste0(target, "_Percentage")]], color = "Males (Data)"),
      size = 2
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = dat_female,
      aes(x = Age, y = .data[[paste0(target, "_Percentage")]], color = "Females (Data)"),
      size = 2
    ) +
    labs(
      title = plottitle,
      x = "Age",
      y = y_label,
      fill = "Legend",
      color = "Legend"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "Females (Data)" = "darkred",
        "Females (SHG)" = "red",
        "Males (Data)" = "darkblue",
        "Males (SHG)" = "blue"
      ),
      breaks = c("Females (Data)", "Females (SHG)", "Males (Data)", "Males (SHG)")  # Controls order in the legend
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = setNames(c("pink", "lightblue"), c(CI_label_f, CI_label_m)),  # Ensure mapping matches dynamic labels
      breaks = c(CI_label_f, CI_label_m)  # Specify order in the legend
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = if (legend == "On") "bottom" else "none",
      legend.box = "horizontal",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 13)
    ) +
    guides(
      color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),  # Two-row legend for lines
      fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)    # Two-row legend for ribbons
    )

  return(plot)
}
```


#prvlnc_plot
Generates two side-by-side plots comparing SHG-simulated and observed smoking prevalence by age and sex for Ever Smokers and Current Smokers. Each plot shows confidence intervals, mean prevalence lines, and data points for males and females. Ensures consistent y-axis limits, distinct color coding, and a single shared legend. Validates input data for required columns to ensure reliable execution.

```{r}
prvlnc_plot <- function(SHG_sim_prvlnc, dat_prvlnc, 
                        legend = "On", subtitle = NULL, population = NULL, CI = 95) {
  # Validate inputs for required columns
  required_cols <- c("Age", "Sex", "EverSmoker_Mean", "EverSmoker_Lower", "EverSmoker_Upper",
                     "SmokeNow_Mean", "SmokeNow_Lower", "SmokeNow_Upper")
  if (!all(required_cols %in% colnames(SHG_sim_prvlnc))) {
    stop("SHG_sim_prvlnc must contain the necessary columns for prevalence analysis.")
  }
  if (!all(c("Age", "Sex", "EverSmoker_Percentage", "SmokeNow_Percentage") %in% colnames(dat_prvlnc))) {
    stop("dat_prvlnc must contain the necessary columns for prevalence analysis.")
  }
  
  # Set up subtitles for the individual plots
  sub1 <- if (!is.null(subtitle)) paste0("Ever Smokers of ", population) else population
  sub2 <- if (!is.null(subtitle)) paste0("Current Smokers of ", population) else population
  
  # Generate the Ever Smokers plot
  plot_ever <- make_prevalence_plot(
    SHG_prvlnc = SHG_sim_prvlnc,
    dat_prvlnc = dat_prvlnc,
    target = "EverSmoker",
    CI = CI,
    legend = legend,
    subtitle = sub1
  )

  # Generate the Current Smokers plot
  plot_now <- make_prevalence_plot(
    SHG_prvlnc = SHG_sim_prvlnc,
    dat_prvlnc = dat_prvlnc,
    target = "SmokeNow",
    CI = CI,
    legend = "Off",  # Suppress individual legends for the second plot
    subtitle = sub2
  )

  # Combine everything with one shared legend
  final_plot <- (plot_ever | plot_now) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +  # Collect all legends into one
    plot_annotation(
      theme = theme(
        legend.position = if (legend == "On") "bottom" else "none",
        legend.box = "horizontal",
        legend.title = element_blank()
      )
    )
  
  # Return the final combined plot
  return(final_plot)
}
```


#dist_plot
This updated dist_plot() function overlays the SHG simulation distribution (blue line with a confidence ribbon) and the observed data distribution (orange line) for a specified variable (CigsPerDay, PackYears, or SmokingYears). Internally, it calls make_data_distribution() to produce either a piecewise-constant bar (for CigsPerDay or SmokingYears) or a kernel density (for PackYears) on the data side. The function then unifies both distributions in a single ggplot object, providing a clear visual comparison of simulation results versus real-world observations.


```{r}
dist_plot <- function(dist_smpled, data, target, 
                      title = "Comparison of Distributions: SHG vs. Data",
                      legend = "On",
                      ytitle = "On",
                      ymax = 0,
                      CI = 95) {
  # Validate input for target
  if (!target %in% c("CigsPerDay", "SmokingYears", "PackYears")) {
    stop("Invalid target. Choose from 'CigsPerDay', 'SmokingYears', or 'PackYears'.")
  }
  
  # --- 1) Identify the SHG columns -----------------------------------------
  var_prefix <- switch(target,
    "CigsPerDay"    = "CigsPerDay",
    "SmokingYears"  = "Smoking_Years",
    "PackYears"     = "Pack_Years"
  )
  mean_col   <- paste0(var_prefix, "_Mean")
  lower_col  <- paste0(var_prefix, "_Lower")
  upper_col  <- paste0(var_prefix, "_Upper")
  
  # Extract SHG y-values
  sampled_mean  <- dist_smpled[[mean_col]]
  sampled_lower <- dist_smpled[[lower_col]]
  sampled_upper <- dist_smpled[[upper_col]]
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # --- 2) Build the "Data" distribution via the helper ---------------------
  # Instead of embedding logic here, call make_data_distribution().
  # This returns a df with columns: x, Data
  data_df <- make_data_distribution(data, target)
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # --- 3) Determine Y-axis limits (ymax) if not specified ------------------
  if (ymax == 0) {
    # Combine data side's "Data" with SHG's upper
    possible_max <- c(data_df$Data, sampled_upper)
    ymax <- max(possible_max, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Prepare CI label for the ribbon
  CI_label <- paste0(CI, "% CI")
  
  # Combine into a single data frame for plotting
  # We'll align x with dist_smpled$x (512 points),
  # and we already have data_df for the data side
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    x         = dist_smpled$x,
    SHG       = sampled_mean,
    SHG_Lower = sampled_lower,
    SHG_Upper = sampled_upper
  )
  
  # --- 4) Build the ggplot ---
  p <- ggplot() +
    # SHG confidence ribbon
    geom_ribbon(
      data = plot_data,
      aes(x = x, ymin = SHG_Lower, ymax = SHG_Upper, fill = CI_label),
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    # SHG mean line
    geom_line(
      data = plot_data,
      aes(x = x, y = SHG, color = "SHG"),
      size = 1
    ) +
    # Data line (bar or density)
    geom_line(
      data = data_df,
      aes(x = x, y = Data, color = "Data"),
      size = 1
    ) +
    # Axis limits
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 80), ylim = c(0, ymax)) +
    # Labels
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = target,
      y = if (ytitle == "On") "Density" else NULL,
      fill = "Legend",
      color = "Legend"
    ) +
    # Fill/color scales
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = setNames("lightblue", CI_label),
      breaks = c(CI_label),
      guide = if (legend == "On") guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.8)) else "none"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("Data" = "orange", "SHG" = "blue"),
      breaks = c("Data", "SHG"),
      guide = if (legend == "On") guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1)) else "none"
    ) +
    # Minimal theme
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.box.background = if (legend == "On") element_rect(color = "black", size = 0.5) else element_blank(),
      legend.box.margin     = if (legend == "On") margin(5, 5, 5, 5) else margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      legend.key.size       = if (legend == "On") unit(1, "lines") else unit(0, "lines"),
      legend.title          = element_blank()
    )
  
  return(p)
}
```


#make_data_distribution
Generates a data-side distribution for plotting, using either a kernel density (for “PackYears”) or a piecewise-constant bar approach (for “CigsPerDay” or “SmokingYears”). The function returns a two-column data frame (x and Data) suitable for overlaying against the SHG distribution in downstream plotting functions.

```{r}
make_data_distribution <- function(data, target) {
  # data: the original data frame (e.g., MECS_sh_cleaned)
  # target: "CigsPerDay", "SmokingYears", or "PackYears"
  # returns a data frame with columns x and Data

  # Filter to valid values
  data_vals <- data[[target]][ data$EverSmoker == 1 & !is.na(data[[target]]) ]

  if (target == "PackYears") {
    # Continuous approach: kernel density
    dd <- density(data_vals, from = 0, to = 100, n = 512)
    data_df <- data.frame(
      x    = dd$x,
      Data = dd$y
    )
  } else {
    # Piecewise-constant bar approach
    if (target == "CigsPerDay") {
      bin_info <- data.frame(
        code  = 1:5,
        xmin  = c(0, 5.1, 10.1, 20.1, 30.1),
        xmax  = c(5, 10, 20, 30, 100)
      )
    } else {
      # SmokingYears
      bin_info <- data.frame(
        code  = 1:5,
        xmin  = c(0, 10.1, 20.1, 30.1, 40.1),
        xmax  = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 100)
      )
    }
    
    tab_code <- table(data_vals)
    sum_codes <- sum(tab_code[names(tab_code) %in% as.character(1:5)])
    
    data_df_list <- list()
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(bin_info))) {
      code_i <- bin_info$code[i]
      if (! code_i %in% names(tab_code)) next
      p_i <- as.numeric(tab_code[as.character(code_i)]) / sum_codes
      width_i <- bin_info$xmax[i] - bin_info$xmin[i]
      height_i <- p_i / width_i
      
      df_i <- data.frame(
        x = c(bin_info$xmin[i], bin_info$xmin[i], bin_info$xmax[i], bin_info$xmax[i], NA),
        Data = c(0, height_i, height_i, 0, NA)
      )
      data_df_list[[i]] <- df_i
    }
    data_df <- do.call(rbind, data_df_list)
  }

  return(data_df)
}
```


#stacked_dist_plots
The stacked_dist_plots function generates and combines distribution comparison plots for CigsPerDay, PackYears, and SmokingYears. It calls the dist_plot function three times, once for each target, and stacks the resulting plots vertically using the patchwork package. The combined plot includes individual titles for each variable as well as an overarching title, providing a clear visualization of the SHG simulations compared to the observed data across key smoking-related variables.

```{r}
# Function to create and stack distribution plots
stacked_dist_plots <- function(dist_smpled, data, 
                               title = "SHG vs. Data: Distributions of Smoking Variables",
                               legend = "On",
                               subtitle = "On",
                               ytitle = "On",
                               ymax = c(0, 0, 0),
                               CI = 95) {
  # Determine subplot titles based on subtitle parameter
  cigs_title <- if (subtitle == "On") "Cigarettes Per Day: SHG vs. Data" else NULL
  packyears_title <- if (subtitle == "On") "Pack Years: SHG vs. Data" else NULL
  smokingyears_title <- if (subtitle == "On") "Smoking Years: SHG vs. Data" else NULL

  # Generate individual plots for each target
  plot_cigs <- dist_plot(
    dist_smpled = dist_smpled,
    data = data,
    target = "CigsPerDay",
    title = cigs_title,
    legend = "Off",
    ytitle = ytitle,
    ymax = ymax[1],
    CI = CI
  )
  
  plot_packyears <- dist_plot(
    dist_smpled = dist_smpled,
    data = data,
    target = "PackYears",
    title = packyears_title,
    legend = "Off",
    ytitle = ytitle,
    ymax = ymax[2],
    CI = CI
  )
  
  plot_smokingyears <- dist_plot(
    dist_smpled = dist_smpled,
    data = data,
    target = "SmokingYears",
    title = smokingyears_title,
    legend = legend,
    ytitle = ytitle,
    ymax = ymax[3],
    CI = CI
  )
  
  # Stack the plots using patchwork
  combined_plot <- plot_cigs / plot_packyears / plot_smokingyears +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1), guides = "collect") + # Equal heights for all plots
    plot_annotation(title)
  
  # Adjust the legend position to the bottom
  combined_plot <- combined_plot & 
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")  # Place the legend explicitly at the bottom
  
  # Return the combined plot
  return(combined_plot)
}
```


#calculate_ymax
This updated calculate_ymax() function determines a single maximum y-axis value for a given variable (CigsPerDay, SmokingYears, or PackYears) by combining peaks from both SHG simulation distributions (_Upper columns) and data distributions. For categorical variables (CigsPerDay or SmokingYears), it calls make_data_distribution() to generate a piecewise bar distribution from the data side and takes its highest bar. For PackYears (continuous), it computes a kernel density on the data side and finds the density’s maximum. The result is the largest y-value across both the data and SHG, ensuring a unified vertical scale in subsequent plots.

```{r}
calculate_ymax <- function(dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, target) {
  # 1) Identify the SHG "_Upper" column
  var_prefix <- switch(target,
    "CigsPerDay"   = "CigsPerDay",
    "SmokingYears" = "Smoking_Years",
    "PackYears"    = "Pack_Years",
    stop("Invalid target. Choose from 'CigsPerDay', 'SmokingYears', or 'PackYears'.")
  )
  
  target_upper <- paste0(var_prefix, "_Upper")
  
  # 2) Extract max SHG peaks from both distributions
  max_shg_1 <- max(dist_smpled_1[[target_upper]], na.rm = TRUE)
  max_shg_2 <- max(dist_smpled_2[[target_upper]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # 3) Determine data maxima
  #    - For PackYears (continuous), do the old density approach
  #    - For CigsPerDay/SmokingYears (categorical), 
  if (target == "CigsPerDay" | target == "SmokingYears") {
    flatdist1 <- make_data_distribution(data_1, target)
    flatdist2 <- make_data_distribution(data_2, target)
    
    data_max_1 <- max(flatdist1$Data, na.rm = TRUE)
    data_max_2 <- max(flatdist2$Data, na.rm = TRUE)
  } else if (target == "PackYears"){
    vals1 <- data_1[[target]][data_1$EverSmoker == 1 & !is.na(data_1[[target]])]
    vals2 <- data_2[[target]][data_2$EverSmoker == 1 & !is.na(data_2[[target]])]
    
    d1 <- density(vals1, from = 0, to = 100, n = 512)
    d2 <- density(vals2, from = 0, to = 100, n = 512)
    data_max_1 <- max(d1$y, na.rm = TRUE)
    data_max_2 <- max(d2$y, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  # 4) Combine and find the overall max
  max_vals <- c(max_shg_1, max_shg_2, data_max_1, data_max_2)
  if (all(is.infinite(max_vals))) return(0)
  return(max(max_vals, na.rm = TRUE))
}
```


#stacked_side_plots
This function generates side-by-side stacked plots comparing smoking variable distributions for two populations. Each column includes subplots for "CigsPerDay", "PackYears", and "SmokingYears", with simulation and data results combined.
Inputs: Simulated distributions (dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2), Observed data (data_1, data_2), Optional column titles (column_titles) and overall title (maintitle).
Output: A combined ggplot object showing side-by-side stacked plots.

```{r}
stacked_side_plots <- function(dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, 
                               maintitle = "Smoking History Distributions: Data vs. SHG", 
                               column_titles = c("Population 1", "Population 2"),
                               CI = 95) {
  # Calculate ymax for each variable
  ymax_cigs <- calculate_ymax(dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, "CigsPerDay")
  ymax_packyears <- calculate_ymax(dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, "PackYears")
  ymax_smokingyears <- calculate_ymax(dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, "SmokingYears")
  ymax <- c(ymax_cigs, ymax_packyears, ymax_smokingyears)
  
  # Generate stacked plots for the first population
  plot_1 <- stacked_dist_plots(
    dist_smpled = dist_smpled_1, 
    data = data_1, 
    title = NULL,
    legend = "On", 
    subtitle = "Off",
    ymax = ymax,
    CI = CI
  )
  
  # Generate stacked plots for the second population
  plot_2 <- stacked_dist_plots(
    dist_smpled = dist_smpled_2, 
    data = data_2, 
    title = NULL,
    legend = "On", 
    subtitle = "Off",
    ytitle = "Off",
    ymax = ymax,
    CI = CI
  )
  
  # Create the column titles as text grobs
  title_main <- ggplot() +
    ggtitle(maintitle) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 13, face = "bold"))
  
  
  title_1 <- ggplot() +
    ggtitle(column_titles[1]) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))
  
  title_2 <- ggplot() +
    ggtitle(column_titles[2]) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))
  
  # Combine column titles and plots
  combined_titles <- title_1 + title_2 + plot_layout(ncol = 2)
  combined_plots <- plot_1 | plot_2
  
  # Combine everything with adjusted layout
  final_plot <- (
    title_main / combined_titles / combined_plots
  ) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(0, 0, 1), guides = "collect") +  # Adjust height for the titles
    plot_annotation(
      theme = theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.box = "horizontal",
        legend.title = element_blank()
      )
    )

  # Return the final combined plot
  return(final_plot)
}
```


#flatten_variable
Creates a piecewise‐constant “bar” distribution for a single variable (CigsPerDay or Smoking_Years) in a 512×N data frame. It calculates the area under each bin, converts that area to a uniform height, and replaces the original _Mean/_Lower/_Upper columns with stepwise values, forcing zero at bin boundaries for a bar‐chart look.

```{r}
flatten_variable <- function(df, var_prefix, bin_info) {
  # var_prefix: e.g. "CigsPerDay" or "Smoking_Years"
  # bin_info: data frame with (xmin, xmax) for each bin
  #
  # This function:
  # 1) Computes bin areas by summing density * dx in each bin
  # 2) Converts those areas into piecewise-constant heights
  # 3) Replaces the original columns with the new stepwise values
  # 4) Forces zero at bin boundaries for a bar chart aesthetic
  
  mean_col  <- paste0(var_prefix, "_Mean")
  lower_col <- paste0(var_prefix, "_Lower")
  upper_col <- paste0(var_prefix, "_Upper")
  
  # If columns don't exist, return df unmodified
  needed_cols <- c(mean_col, lower_col, upper_col)
  if (!all(needed_cols %in% names(df))) {
    return(df)
  }
  
  # 1) Prepare for bin area calculation
  x <- df$x
  n <- length(x)
  var_mean  <- df[[mean_col]]
  var_lower <- df[[lower_col]]
  var_upper <- df[[upper_col]]
  
  # dx for each interval
  dx <- numeric(n)
  for (j in seq_len(n-1)) {
    dx[j] <- x[j+1] - x[j]
  }
  dx[n] <- 0
  
  # Create storage for bin areas
  bin_area_mean  <- numeric(nrow(bin_info))
  bin_area_lower <- numeric(nrow(bin_info))
  bin_area_upper <- numeric(nrow(bin_info))
  
  # 2) Accumulate area in each bin
  for (j in seq_len(n-1)) {
    xm <- x[j]
    i_bin <- which(xm >= bin_info$xmin & xm < bin_info$xmax)
    if (length(i_bin) == 1) {
      bin_area_mean[i_bin]  <- bin_area_mean[i_bin]  + var_mean[j]  * dx[j]
      bin_area_lower[i_bin] <- bin_area_lower[i_bin] + var_lower[j] * dx[j]
      bin_area_upper[i_bin] <- bin_area_upper[i_bin] + var_upper[j] * dx[j]
    }
  }
  
  # 3) Compute bin heights = area / width
  bin_width    <- bin_info$xmax - bin_info$xmin
  height_mean  <- bin_area_mean  / bin_width
  height_lower <- bin_area_lower / bin_width
  height_upper <- bin_area_upper / bin_width
  
  # 4) Overwrite the original columns with stepwise values
  # We'll define new vectors for the variable
  new_mean  <- numeric(n)
  new_lower <- numeric(n)
  new_upper <- numeric(n)
  
  for (j in seq_len(n)) {
    xm <- x[j]
    
    # Check if x[j] is a boundary
    is_boundary <- any(abs(xm - bin_info$xmin) < 1e-9) | 
                   any(abs(xm - bin_info$xmax) < 1e-9)
    if (is_boundary) {
      # Force zero at the boundary for a vertical drop
      new_mean[j]  <- 0
      new_lower[j] <- 0
      new_upper[j] <- 0
    } else {
      i_bin <- which(xm > bin_info$xmin & xm < bin_info$xmax)
      if (length(i_bin) == 1) {
        new_mean[j]  <- height_mean[i_bin]
        new_lower[j] <- height_lower[i_bin]
        new_upper[j] <- height_upper[i_bin]
      } else {
        # outside or exactly on boundary
        new_mean[j]  <- 0
        new_lower[j] <- 0
        new_upper[j] <- 0
      }
    }
  }
  
  df[[mean_col]]  <- new_mean
  df[[lower_col]] <- new_lower
  df[[upper_col]] <- new_upper
  
  return(df)
}
```


#flatten_distribution
Applies flatten_variable() to a full distribution data frame (e.g., 512×10), transforming the CigsPerDay and Smoking_Years columns into bar‐style step functions. It leaves Pack_Years columns unchanged, returning a data frame of the same shape that can be plotted as piecewise bars for those two variables.

```{r}
flatten_distribution <- function(dist_df) {
  # dist_df: 512 x 10 data frame with:
  #   x
  #   CigsPerDay_Mean/_Lower/_Upper
  #   Pack_Years_Mean/_Lower/_Upper
  #   Smoking_Years_Mean/_Lower/_Upper
  
  # We'll define bin_info for CigsPerDay & Smoking_Years
  bin_info_cpd <- data.frame(
    xmin = c(0,  5.1, 10.1, 20.1, 30.1),
    xmax = c(5, 10,   20,   30,   100)
  )
  bin_info_sy <- data.frame(
    xmin = c(0,  10.1, 20.1, 30.1, 40.1),
    xmax = c(10, 20,   30,   40,   100)
  )
  
  # 1) Flatten "CigsPerDay" columns
  dist_df <- flatten_variable(dist_df, "CigsPerDay", bin_info_cpd)
  
  # 2) Flatten "Smoking_Years" columns
  dist_df <- flatten_variable(dist_df, "Smoking_Years", bin_info_sy)
  
  # 3) Leave Pack_Years columns unchanged
  return(dist_df)
}
```


#dist_plot_2
This function compares the observed MECS smoking-history distribution for one variable against the corresponding flattened SHG mean density and confidence interval. It returns a single ggplot object with the standardized styling used across the cohort files while preserving the MECS flattening workflow.

```{r}
dist_plot_2 <- function(dist_smpled, data, target, 
                        title = "Comparison of Distributions: SHG vs. Data",
                        legend = "On",
                        ytitle = "On",
                        ymax = 0,
                        CI = 95) {
  
  if (!target %in% c("CigsPerDay", "PackYears", "SmokingYears")) {
    stop("Invalid target. Choose from 'CigsPerDay', 'PackYears', or 'SmokingYears'.")
  }

  # Column mappings for SHG
  target_cols <- switch(target,
    CigsPerDay   = c("CigsPerDay_Mean", "CigsPerDay_Lower", "CigsPerDay_Upper"),
    PackYears    = c("Pack_Years_Mean", "Pack_Years_Lower", "Pack_Years_Upper"),
    SmokingYears = c("Smoking_Years_Mean", "Smoking_Years_Lower", "Smoking_Years_Upper")
  )
  
  x_label <- switch(target,
    CigsPerDay   = "Cigarettes Per Day",
    PackYears    = "Pack-Years",
    SmokingYears = "Smoking Duration (Years)"
  )

  # SHG distribution is already flattened to the MECS category structure upstream.
  sampled_mean  <- dist_smpled[[target_cols[1]]]
  sampled_lower <- dist_smpled[[target_cols[2]]]
  sampled_upper <- dist_smpled[[target_cols[3]]]
  x_vals <- dist_smpled$x

  # Observed MECS distribution is flattened to the same x grid for direct comparison.
  data_df <- make_data_distribution(data, target)
  
  if (ymax == 0) {
    ymax <- max(c(data_df$Data, sampled_upper), na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  CI_label <- paste0(CI, "% CI")
  
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    x         = x_vals,
    SHG       = sampled_mean,
    SHG_Lower = sampled_lower,
    SHG_Upper = sampled_upper
  )

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_ribbon(
      data = plot_data,
      aes(x = x, ymin = SHG_Lower, ymax = SHG_Upper, fill = CI_label),
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = plot_data,
      aes(x = x, y = SHG, color = "SHG"),
      linewidth = 1.3
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = data_df,
      aes(x = x, y = Data, color = "MECS"),
      linewidth = 1.3
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02)),
      limits = c(0, ymax),
      labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.01)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 80), ylim = c(0, ymax)) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = x_label,
      y = if (ytitle == "On") "Density" else NULL,
      fill = "Legend",
      color = "Legend"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("MECS" = "orange", "SHG" = "blue"),
      breaks = c("MECS", "SHG"),
      labels = c("MECS (observed)", "SHG (simulated)")
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = setNames("lightblue", CI_label),
      breaks = c(CI_label)
    ) +
    guides(
      color = if (legend == "On") guide_legend(order = 1) else "none",
      fill  = if (legend == "On") guide_legend(order = 2) else "none"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
    theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.title.x    = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.title.y    = element_text(size = 16),
      axis.text       = element_text(size = 14),
      legend.text     = element_text(size = 14),
      legend.title    = element_blank(),
      legend.position = if (legend == "On") "bottom" else "none",
      axis.line       = element_line(color = "black"),
      panel.border    = element_blank(),
      plot.margin     = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )

  return(p)
}
```


#stacked_dist_plots_2
This function builds the three single-variable MECS-versus-SHG distribution comparisons from dist_plot_2 and returns them as a named list. It allows the caller to control subtitles, legend placement, shared y-axis scaling, and whether the x-axis is shown on each component plot.

```{r}
stacked_dist_plots_2 <- function(dist_smpled, data, 
                                 subtitle = "On",
                                 ytitle = "On",
                                 ymax = c(0, 0, 0),
                                 CI = 95,
                                 legend_flags = c("Off", "Off", "Off"),
                                 show_x_axis = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)) {
  # Helper to strip x-axis for stacked layout
  strip_x <- function(p) {
    p + theme(
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    ) + xlab(NULL)
  }

  titles <- if (subtitle == "On") {
    c("Cigarettes Per Day: SHG vs. Data", "Pack Years: SHG vs. Data", "Smoking Years: SHG vs. Data")
  } else {
    rep(NULL, 3)
  }

  # Cigs plot
  plot_cigs <- dist_plot_2(
    dist_smpled = dist_smpled,
    data        = data,
    target      = "CigsPerDay",
    title       = titles[1],
    legend      = legend_flags[1],
    ytitle      = ytitle,
    ymax        = ymax[1],
    CI          = CI
  )
  if (!show_x_axis[1]) plot_cigs <- strip_x(plot_cigs)

  # PackYears plot
  plot_packyears <- dist_plot_2(
    dist_smpled = dist_smpled,
    data        = data,
    target      = "PackYears",
    title       = titles[2],
    legend      = legend_flags[2],
    ytitle      = ytitle,
    ymax        = ymax[2],
    CI          = CI
  )
  if (!show_x_axis[2]) plot_packyears <- strip_x(plot_packyears)

  # SmokingYears plot
  plot_smokingyears <- dist_plot_2(
    dist_smpled = dist_smpled,
    data        = data,
    target      = "SmokingYears",
    title       = titles[3],
    legend      = legend_flags[3],
    ytitle      = ytitle,
    ymax        = ymax[3],
    CI          = CI
  )
  if (!show_x_axis[3]) plot_smokingyears <- strip_x(plot_smokingyears)

  return(list(
    cigs         = plot_cigs,
    packyears    = plot_packyears,
    smokingyears = plot_smokingyears
  ))
}
```


#stacked_plots
This function arranges two groups of MECS-versus-SHG distribution plots into a single stacked figure with optional shared title and legend. It standardizes y-axis limits across the paired groups so differences between rows can be compared on the same scale.

```{r}
stacked_plots <- function(
  dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, 
  maintitle = "Smoking History Distributions: SHG vs. Data", 
  row_titles = c("Group 1", "Group 2"),
  CI = 95,
  include_title = TRUE,
  include_legend = TRUE
) {
  # Calculate ymax
  ymax <- c(
    calculate_ymax(dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, "CigsPerDay"),
    calculate_ymax(dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, "PackYears"),
    calculate_ymax(dist_smpled_1, dist_smpled_2, data_1, data_2, "SmokingYears")
  )

  # Extract legend if needed
  if (include_legend) {
    legend_plot <- dist_plot_2(
      dist_smpled = dist_smpled_1,
      data = data_1,
      target = "SmokingYears",
      title = NULL,
      legend = "On",
      ytitle = "Off",
      ymax = ymax[3],
      CI = CI
    ) + theme(
      legend.text = element_text(size = 20),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.direction = "horizontal",
      legend.background = element_blank(),
      legend.box.background = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      plot.background = element_blank()
    )
    legend_shared <- get_legend(legend_plot)
  }

  # Top row (no x-axis)
  plots_pop1 <- stacked_dist_plots_2(
    dist_smpled_1, data_1,
    subtitle = "Off", ytitle = "Off", ymax = ymax, CI = CI,
    legend_flags = c("Off", "Off", "Off"),
    show_x_axis = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
  )

  # Bottom row (with x-axis)
  plots_pop2 <- stacked_dist_plots_2(
    dist_smpled_2, data_2,
    subtitle = "Off", ytitle = "Off", ymax = ymax, CI = CI,
    legend_flags = c("Off", "Off", "Off"),
    show_x_axis = if (include_legend) c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE) else c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
  )

  # Rows of plots
  row1 <- plot_grid(plots_pop1$cigs, plots_pop1$packyears, plots_pop1$smokingyears, ncol = 3)
  row2 <- plot_grid(plots_pop2$cigs, plots_pop2$packyears, plots_pop2$smokingyears, ncol = 3)

  # Row labels (rotated inward)
  row_label_1 <- ggdraw() + draw_label(row_titles[1], angle = 270, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 20)
  row_label_2 <- ggdraw() + draw_label(row_titles[2], angle = 270, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 20)

  # Add row labels to right
  row1_labeled <- plot_grid(row1, row_label_1, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(1, 0.05), align = "v")
  row2_labeled <- plot_grid(row2, row_label_2, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(1, 0.05), align = "v")

  # Stack rows
  plot_body <- plot_grid(
    row1_labeled,
    row2_labeled,
    ncol = 1,
    rel_heights = if (include_legend) c(1, 1.3) else c(1, 1),
    align = "v"
  )
  # Title and layout
  title_main <- ggdraw() + draw_label(maintitle, fontface = "bold", size = 22, hjust = 0.5)

  plot_list <- list()
  if (include_title) plot_list <- c(plot_list, list(title_main))
  plot_list <- c(plot_list, list(plot_body))
  if (include_legend) plot_list <- c(plot_list, list(legend_shared))

  rel_heights <- c()
  if (include_title) rel_heights <- c(rel_heights, 0.06)
  rel_heights <- c(rel_heights, 1)
  if (include_legend) rel_heights <- c(rel_heights, 0.12)

  final_plot <- plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list, ncol = 1, rel_heights = rel_heights)
  return(final_plot)
}
```


#count_eligible
The count_eligible function calculates the number of individuals meeting smoking screening criteria based on age and smoking history. It filters the dataset to include those within a specified age range who meet or exceed a given threshold for a smoking measure (e.g., Pack Years or Smoking Years). It considers both current smokers and former smokers who quit within the last 15 years (YSQ ≤ 15), returning the total count of eligible individuals.

```{r}
# Helper function for eligibility criteria
count_eligible <- function(df, measure, threshold, min_age, max_age = 80, 
                           age_col, smoker_col) {
  df %>%
    filter(.data[[age_col]] >= min_age, .data[[age_col]] <= max_age, 
           .data[[measure]] >= threshold, 
           (.data[[smoker_col]] == 1 | (.data[[smoker_col]] == 0 & YSQ <= 15))) %>%
    nrow()
}
``` 


#screening_eligible
The screening_eligible function calculates key smoking-related statistics for a given dataset, distinguishing between simulated SHG data and observed cohort data. It computes the total population, the number of ever-smokers, current smokers, and former smokers. Additionally, it determines the prevalence of individuals exceeding pack-year and smoking-year thresholds (PY≥20, PY≥30, SY≥20, SY≥30) and assesses eligibility for lung cancer screening based on 2021 and 2013 USPSTF guidelines, as well as alternative SY-based criteria. The function returns these values in a structured dataframe.

```{r}
screening_eligible <- function(df, dataset_type = "SHG") {
  # Validate dataset_type
  if (!dataset_type %in% c("SHG", "MECS")) {
    stop("Invalid dataset_type. Use 'SHG' for simulated data or 'MECS' for real data.")
  }

  # Define column mappings for SHG vs MECS
  if (dataset_type == "SHG") {
    age_col       <- "Age"
    smoker_col    <- "Smokenow"
    ever_col      <- "Eversmoker"
    cessation_col <- "Cessation_Age"
    py_col        <- "Pack_Years"
    sy_col        <- "Smoking_Years"
  } else {  # dataset_type refers to observed cohort data
    age_col <- "Enrollment_Age"
    smoker_col <- "SmokeNow"
    ever_col <- "EverSmoker"
    cessation_col <- "AgeQuitSmoking"
    py_col <- "PackYears"
    sy_col <- "SmokingYears"
  }

  # If MECS, convert smkyrs + smkquit to numeric midpoints
  if (dataset_type == "MECS") {
    df <- df %>%
      mutate(
        # Convert smkyrs (codes 1..5) into numeric midpoints for SmokingYears
        SmokingYears = case_when(
          smkyrs == 1 ~ 10,  # ≤10 years
          smkyrs == 2 ~ 15,  # 11-20 years => midpoint ~15
          smkyrs == 3 ~ 25,  # 21-30 years => 25
          smkyrs == 4 ~ 35,  # 31-40 => 35
          smkyrs == 5 ~ 45,  # ≥41 => 45
          TRUE ~ NA_real_
        ),
        # Convert smkquit (codes 1..7) into numeric midpoints for YSQ
        # If smoker_col == 1 => current smoker => YSQ=0
        YSQ = case_when(
          .data[[smoker_col]] == 1 ~ 0,  
          smkquit == 1 ~ 0.5,  # <1 year
          smkquit == 2 ~ 1.5,  # 1-2 years
          smkquit == 3 ~ 4,    # 3-5 years
          smkquit == 4 ~ 8,    # 6-10 years
          smkquit == 5 ~ 13,   # 11-15 years
          smkquit == 6 ~ 18,   # 16-20 years
          smkquit == 7 ~ 25,   # 21+ years
          TRUE ~ NA_real_
        )
      )
  } else {
    # If SHG or an observed cohort dataset, compute YSQ from Age - Cessation_Age
    df <- df %>%
      mutate(YSQ = case_when(
        .data[[smoker_col]] == 1 ~ 0,  # Current smokers => YSQ=0
        .data[[smoker_col]] == 0 & .data[[cessation_col]] > 0 ~ .data[[age_col]] - .data[[cessation_col]],
        .data[[smoker_col]] == 0 & .data[[cessation_col]] <= 0 ~ NA_real_
      ))
  }

  # Count populations
  total_population <- nrow(df)
  ever_smokers <- df %>% filter(.data[[ever_col]] == 1)
  count_eversmokers <- nrow(ever_smokers)
  count_currentsmokers <- 
    nrow(ever_smokers %>% filter(.data[[smoker_col]] == 1))
  count_formersmokers <- 
    count_eversmokers - count_currentsmokers  # EverSmoker = Current + Former

  # Compute prevalence of PY≥20, PY≥30, SY≥20, SY≥30
  prevalence_counts <- c(
    PY20 = nrow(ever_smokers %>% filter(.data[[py_col]] >= 20)),
    PY30 = nrow(ever_smokers %>% filter(.data[[py_col]] >= 30)),
    SY20 = nrow(ever_smokers %>% filter(.data[[sy_col]] >= 20)),
    SY30 = nrow(ever_smokers %>% filter(.data[[sy_col]] >= 30))
  )

  # Compute eligibility counts using the external helper function
  eligibility_counts <- c(
    Eligible_2021 = count_eligible(df = ever_smokers, 
                                   measure = py_col, 
                                   threshold = 20, 
                                   min_age = 50,
                                   max_age = 80,
                                   age_col = age_col,
                                   smoker_col = smoker_col),
    Eligible_2013 = count_eligible(df = ever_smokers, 
                                   measure = py_col, 
                                   threshold = 30, 
                                   min_age = 55,
                                   max_age = 80,
                                   age_col = age_col,
                                   smoker_col = smoker_col),
    Eligible_SY20 = count_eligible(df = ever_smokers, 
                                   measure = sy_col, 
                                   threshold = 20, 
                                   min_age = 50,
                                   max_age = 80,
                                   age_col = age_col,
                                   smoker_col = smoker_col),
    Eligible_SY30 = count_eligible(df = ever_smokers, 
                                   measure = sy_col, 
                                   threshold = 30, 
                                   min_age = 50,
                                   max_age = 80,
                                   age_col = age_col,
                                   smoker_col = smoker_col)
  )

  # Return structured dataframe
  data.frame(
    Dataset         = dataset_type,
    Total_Population= total_population,
    EverSmokers     = count_eversmokers,
    CurrentSmokers  = count_currentsmokers,
    FormerSmokers   = count_formersmokers,
    PY20            = prevalence_counts["PY20"],
    PY30            = prevalence_counts["PY30"],
    SY20            = prevalence_counts["SY20"],
    SY30            = prevalence_counts["SY30"],
    Eligible_2021   = eligibility_counts["Eligible_2021"],
    Eligible_2013   = eligibility_counts["Eligible_2013"],
    Eligible_SY20   = eligibility_counts["Eligible_SY20"],
    Eligible_SY30   = eligibility_counts["Eligible_SY30"]
  )
}
```


#aggregate_screening
The aggregate_screening function processes repeated screening eligibility assessments across multiple samples and summarizes key statistics. It calculates the mean, lower, and upper confidence bounds for total population, ever-smokers, current smokers, former smokers, and individuals exceeding specific pack-year (PY) and smoking-year (SY) thresholds. Additionally, it aggregates eligibility estimates based on 2021 and 2013 USPSTF criteria, as well as SY-based alternatives. The function returns a structured dataframe with the population name as the first column.

```{r}
aggregate_screening <- function(screening_data, subpop_name, CI = 0.95) {
  df <- bind_rows(screening_data)
  
  df_summary <- df %>%
    summarise(
      Total_Population = mean(Total_Population),
      
      EverSmokers_Mean = mean(EverSmokers),
      EverSmokers_Lower = quantile(EverSmokers, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      EverSmokers_Upper = quantile(EverSmokers, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),
      
      CurrentSmokers_Mean = mean(CurrentSmokers),
      CurrentSmokers_Lower = quantile(CurrentSmokers, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      CurrentSmokers_Upper = quantile(CurrentSmokers, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),
      
      FormerSmokers_Mean = mean(FormerSmokers),
      FormerSmokers_Lower = quantile(FormerSmokers, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      FormerSmokers_Upper = quantile(FormerSmokers, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),
      
      PY20_Mean = mean(PY20),
      PY20_Lower = quantile(PY20, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      PY20_Upper = quantile(PY20, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),

      PY30_Mean = mean(PY30),
      PY30_Lower = quantile(PY30, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      PY30_Upper = quantile(PY30, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),

      SY20_Mean = mean(SY20),
      SY20_Lower = quantile(SY20, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      SY20_Upper = quantile(SY20, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),

      SY30_Mean = mean(SY30),
      SY30_Lower = quantile(SY30, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      SY30_Upper = quantile(SY30, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),

      Eligible_2021_Mean = mean(Eligible_2021),
      Eligible_2021_Lower = quantile(Eligible_2021, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      Eligible_2021_Upper = quantile(Eligible_2021, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),

      Eligible_2013_Mean = mean(Eligible_2013),
      Eligible_2013_Lower = quantile(Eligible_2013, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      Eligible_2013_Upper = quantile(Eligible_2013, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),

      Eligible_SY20_Mean = mean(Eligible_SY20),
      Eligible_SY20_Lower = quantile(Eligible_SY20, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      Eligible_SY20_Upper = quantile(Eligible_SY20, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2),

      Eligible_SY30_Mean = mean(Eligible_SY30),
      Eligible_SY30_Lower = quantile(Eligible_SY30, probs = (1 - CI) / 2),
      Eligible_SY30_Upper = quantile(Eligible_SY30, probs = 1 - (1 - CI) / 2)
    ) %>%
    mutate(Population = subpop_name) %>%
    select(Population, everything())  # Ensure Population is first column

  return(df_summary)
}
```


#rep_smpl_screening
The rep_smpl_screening function performs repeated sampling from a simulated population and evaluates screening eligibility across different subpopulations.
